meta.title: Regime changes and state formation/dissolution, 1836–1991
meta.scope: Selected major powers, successor states and major 20th-century regime transitions; not an exhaustive world chronology. Additional law milestones added for Russian emancipation (1861), Finnish equal suffrage (1906), and social-insurance/welfare reforms (US 1935; UK NHS 1948).
meta.schemaNote: Research staging only. `entityBefore/After.id` values are historical or proposed identifiers; IDs not present in political_entities/registry.json are marked in mapping notes in the companion report. `capitalHistorical` is a city name, not an engine region ID. `lawChanges` only uses current enum values when known; concepts needing new enum values are in `proposedLawChanges` and `proposedLaws`.
meta.dateConvention: ISO-8601 Gregorian dates. Where an event is a process, windowStart/windowEnd delimit the transition; the `date` field is the principal legal/proclamation milestone.

qualityLegend.verified: Official primary/legal/archival source confirms date or text.
qualityLegend.supported: Credible institutional or academic secondary source; some interpretation remains.
qualityLegend.unverified: Not used for core dates; explicit gaps are noted in report.

proposedLaws.description: A single ruling party holds a constitutionally or practically exclusive position in national political power.
A ruling party monopolises political authority and bans or suppresses opposition parties.

proposedLaws.name_vi: Phổ thông đầu phiếu phổ quát
proposedLaws.description: Adult citizens can vote irrespective of sex; use instead of the current male-only universal_suffrage enum.

proposedLaws.name_vi: Cộng hòa tổng thống đa đảng
proposedLaws.description: Competitive parties, elected executive presidency and constitutional checks.
Executive authority concentrated in a leader; legislature and electoral accountability suspended.
President has independent constitutional powers alongside a government accountable to parliament.
Formal state title may remain republican or monarchical while actual constitutional government is replaced by executive dictatorship.

proposedLaws.name_vi: Kinh tế kế hoạch hóa tập trung
proposedLaws.description: State ownership of strategic productive assets and binding central plans allocate investment, output and inputs.

proposedLaws.name_vi: Kinh tế xã hội chủ nghĩa nhà nước
proposedLaws.description: Land and major industry placed under state or collective ownership, before the mature command-planning system.

proposedLaws.name_vi: Chuyển đổi kinh tế thị trường trong khuôn khổ xã hội chủ nghĩa
proposedLaws.description: Limited markets, enterprise autonomy and private/cooperative activity introduced while party-state control remains.

proposedLaws.name_vi: Nhà nước độc quyền ngoại thương
proposedLaws.description: Foreign trade and foreign-exchange access are administered through state monopolies and plans.

proposedLaws.name_vi: Hệ thống lao động do nhà nước điều phối
proposedLaws.description: Employment allocation and labour mobility are substantially controlled by the state; coercive practices must be separately represented.

proposedLaws.name_vi: Từ bỏ chiến tranh theo hiến pháp
proposedLaws.description: Constitutional prohibition on war and maintaining war potential; distinct from ordinary army size or conscription laws.

proposedLaws.name_vi: Hệ tư tưởng nhà nước cộng sản
proposedLaws.description: Official Marxist-Leninist or Communist Party ideology; track separately from ownership and the party-system law.

proposedLaws.name_vi: Hệ tư tưởng nhà nước phát xít
proposedLaws.description: Ultranationalist, authoritarian, anti-liberal state ideology; do not conflate all authoritarian regimes with fascism.
Racial hierarchy, Führer principle and genocidal expansionism; separate from generic fascist or authoritarian ideology.

proposedLaws.name_vi: Bảo hiểm xã hội và nhà nước phúc lợi
proposedLaws.description: Public pensions, unemployment insurance, family support and social protection; cross-cutting social-policy dimension rather than a substitute for economy ownership.

proposedLaws.name_vi: Quyền công dân và bầu cử bình đẳng
proposedLaws.description: Women and men have equal political rights, including voting and eligibility for elected office; distinguish legal suffrage from broader equality.

entityBefore.name_vi: Đế quốc Nga

entityAfter.name_en: Russian Empire under the Fundamental Laws
entityAfter.name_vi: Đế quốc Nga theo Luật Cơ bản

causes: Defeat in the Russo-Japanese War
The 1905 Revolution and mass strikes

power.note: The October Manifesto promised civil liberties and an elected Duma; it did not create parliamentary sovereignty or end autocracy.

press.note: Temporary easing followed, but censorship and repression persisted.

events.note: Do not model as a full constitutional monarchy. The 1906 Fundamental Laws retained the Emperor's dominant executive and legislative powers.

entityBefore.name_vi: Vương quốc Pháp (Quân chủ tháng Bảy)

entityAfter.name_vi: Đệ nhị Cộng hòa Pháp

causes: Banquet campaign and political exclusion
Economic crisis and urban unrest

power.note: Universal male suffrage was decreed in March 1848.

events.note: Republic proclaimed at Paris City Hall on 24 February; Constituent Assembly formally proclaimed it on 4 May 1848.

entityBefore.name_vi: Đệ nhị Cộng hòa Pháp

entityAfter.name_vi: Đệ nhị Đế chế Pháp

causes: Louis-Napoléon Bonaparte's coup of 2 December 1851
Constitutional deadlock over presidential re-election

power.note: Plebiscitary legitimacy remained, but executive power was concentrated in Napoleon III.

events.note: The coup occurred 2 December 1851; the Empire was proclaimed after the plebiscite on 2 December 1852.

entityBefore.name_vi: Đệ nhị Đế chế Pháp

entityAfter.name_vi: Đệ tam Cộng hòa Pháp

causes: French defeat at Sedan in the Franco-Prussian War
Capture of Napoleon III and collapse of imperial authority

power.note: Universal male suffrage survived from 1848; republican institutions were consolidated over several years.

territorialChanges.note: Treaty of Frankfurt; territorial loss followed the 1870–71 defeat.

events.note: Republic proclaimed 4 September 1870; constitutional laws establishing its institutions were adopted in 1875.

entityBefore.name_vi: Đệ tam Cộng hòa Pháp

entityAfter.name_vi: Nhà nước Pháp (Vichy)

causes: Military defeat and armistice with Germany
Collapse of the Third Republic's wartime government

power.note: Parliament transferred constituent powers to Pétain; elected chambers were then adjourned.

governance.note: Vichy formally styled itself État français; do not treat as a normal constitutional republic.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Nhà nước độc tài
proposedLawChanges.description: Executive sovereignty concentrated in a leader; elected legislature suspended.

territorialChanges.to: Vichy administration in unoccupied zone; German military occupation in north and west
territorialChanges.note: Split sovereignty and occupation; Free France continued the war outside Vichy control.

events.note: 10 July 1940 is the full-powers vote; first constitutional acts on 11 July created the authoritarian Vichy order. Vichy was not simply the whole of France.

entityBefore.name_vi: Nhà nước Pháp (Vichy)

entityAfter.name_en: Provisional Government of the French Republic
entityAfter.name_vi: Chính phủ Lâm thời Cộng hòa Pháp

causes: Allied liberation of France
Free France and Resistance institutions claimed republican legitimacy

power.note: Women voted in the 1945 elections; suffrage became universal adult suffrage.

events.note: The CFLN was formed in Algiers on 3 June 1943 and became the GPRF on 3 June 1944; Paris was liberated on 25 August 1944. The GPRF governed until the Fourth Republic.

entityBefore.name_en: Provisional Government of the French Republic
entityBefore.name_vi: Chính phủ Lâm thời Cộng hòa Pháp

entityAfter.name_vi: Đệ tứ Cộng hòa Pháp

causes: Post-war constituent process
Referendum approval of the Constitution
events.note: Constitution promulgated 27 October 1946; Fourth Republic's institutional period conventionally begins 16 January 1947 in the National Assembly chronology.

entityBefore.name_vi: Đệ tứ Cộng hòa Pháp

entityAfter.name_vi: Đệ ngũ Cộng hòa Pháp

causes: Algerian crisis and May 1958 political-military crisis
Collapse of Fourth Republic government

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Cộng hòa bán tổng thống
proposedLawChanges.description: President with substantial constitutional powers alongside a Prime Minister responsible to Parliament.

events.note: Constitution approved by referendum 28 September and promulgated 4 October 1958.

entityBefore.name_en: Kingdom of Prussia and North German Confederation
entityBefore.name_vi: Vương quốc Phổ và Liên bang Bắc Đức

entityAfter.name_vi: Đế quốc Đức

causes: Prussian victory over Austria in 1866
North German Confederation and southern German states joined after Franco-Prussian War

power.note: Reichstag elected by universal male suffrage; executive power remained with Emperor and Chancellor.

territorialChanges.territory: German states north and south of Main
territorialChanges.note: Bavaria, Württemberg, Baden and Hesse joined; Austria excluded.

events.note: The new Empire was founded legally on 1 January 1871; Wilhelm I was proclaimed Emperor at Versailles on 18 January. Use 18 January for public proclamation, 1 January for legal foundation.

entityBefore.name_vi: Đế quốc Đức

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Đức (Cộng hòa Weimar)

causes: Military defeat in World War I
Kiel sailors' mutiny and November Revolution
Kaiser Wilhelm II abdicated

power.note: Women gained national voting rights in 1918; universal suffrage was extended.

events.note: Republic proclaimed 9 November 1918; Weimar Constitution signed 11 August 1919. Germany's 1918 revolution is distinct from the 1919 constitutional settlement.

entityBefore.name_vi: Cộng hòa Weimar

entityAfter.name_en: German Reich under National Socialist rule
entityAfter.name_vi: Đế chế Đức dưới chế độ Quốc xã

causes: Great Depression and mass unemployment
Fragmented parliamentary coalitions and emergency rule
Hitler appointed Chancellor; Enabling Act dismantled constitutional checks

governance.note: The state retained the Reich name and formal republican shell; actual government became a Führer dictatorship.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Độc tài độc đảng
proposedLawChanges.description: All opposition parties banned; ruling party monopolises political power.

events.note: 30 January 1933 marks appointment, not instant completion; Enabling Act 23 March 1933 and subsequent coordination destroyed democracy.

entityBefore.name_en: German Reich under National Socialist rule
entityBefore.name_vi: Đế chế Đức dưới chế độ Quốc xã

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Liên bang Đức

causes: Unconditional German surrender and four-power occupation
Cold War division between Western Allies and Soviet Union

power.note: Federal elections included women; the 1949 Basic Law established democratic institutions.

territorialChanges.note: Separate record GER-1949-10 captures the GDR.

events.note: FRG founded 23 May 1949; this record does not imply it alone represented all German territory.

entityBefore.name_vi: Vùng chiếm đóng của Liên Xô tại Đức

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Dân chủ Đức

causes: Cold War confrontation and failure to agree on an all-German settlement
Soviet-backed constitutional process in the eastern occupation zone

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Nhà nước độc đảng
proposedLawChanges.description: SED-led political monopoly; formally front parties and mass organisations remained.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Kinh tế kế hoạch hóa tập trung
proposedLawChanges.description: State ownership and binding central production plans.

events.note: GDR formation date 7 October 1949; it ceased to exist when it acceded to the FRG on 3 October 1990.

entityBefore.name_vi: Cộng hòa Dân chủ Đức

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Liên bang Đức (thống nhất)

causes: Peaceful Revolution in East Germany
Fall of Berlin Wall and negotiations among Two Plus Four powers

territorialChanges.territory: GDR territory (five Länder and East Berlin)
territorialChanges.note: GDR acceded to the FRG; not a merger of two equal sovereign states under a new constitution.

events.note: German unity became effective 3 October 1990; Basic Law extended to the former GDR.

entityBefore.name_en: Kingdom of Sardinia and Italian states
entityBefore.name_vi: Vương quốc Sardinia và các quốc gia Ý

entityAfter.name_vi: Vương quốc Ý

causes: Risorgimento nationalist movement
Second Italian War of Independence and Garibaldi's Expedition of the Thousand

power.note: The Statuto Albertino was extended; electorate remained narrow.

territorialChanges.territory: Most Italian states and Kingdom of Two Sicilies

events.note: Kingdom proclaimed 17 March 1861; Rome was taken in 1870 and became capital in 1871. Italian unification was a multi-stage process.

entityBefore.name_vi: Vương quốc Ý (quân chủ lập hiến)

entityAfter.name_en: Kingdom of Italy under Fascist dictatorship
entityAfter.name_vi: Vương quốc Ý dưới chế độ độc tài Phát xít

causes: Post-war social conflict and political violence
March on Rome; King Victor Emmanuel III appointed Mussolini Prime Minister

governance.note: The monarchy remained; the Fascist Party destroyed parliamentary democracy.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Độc tài độc đảng
proposedLawChanges.description: Fascist Party monopolises political authority; opposition suppressed.

events.note: Mussolini was appointed on 30 October 1922; consolidation into dictatorship took several years, especially 1925–26.

entityBefore.name_en: Kingdom of Italy under Fascist/post-war transition
entityBefore.name_vi: Vương quốc Ý thời hậu Phát xít

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Ý

causes: Fall of Fascism and end of monarchy's wartime legitimacy
Institutional referendum on 2 June 1946 chose a republic

power.note: Women voted in the 1946 referendum and Constituent Assembly election; use proposed universal_suffrage because current enum is male-specific.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Phổ thông đầu phiếu phổ quát
proposedLawChanges.description: Voting rights for adult citizens irrespective of sex.

events.note: The referendum was held 2 June; the republic was officially proclaimed 18 June. Constitution entered into force 1 January 1948.

entityBefore.name_vi: Đế quốc Áo

entityAfter.name_vi: Quân chủ Áo-Hungary

causes: Austrian defeat in the Austro-Prussian War of 1866
Hungarian political pressure for restoration of constitutional autonomy

power.note: Dualist constitutional institutions; franchise remained restricted and unequal.

territorialChanges.territory: Kingdom of Hungary and associated lands
territorialChanges.to: Hungarian Crown lands with separate parliament and government under shared monarch

events.note: Ausgleich signed 15 March 1867; Hungarian coronation and constitutional settlement followed in June. The monarchy had two constituent halves, not a unitary state with simple provinces.

events.capitalHistorical: Vienna and Budapest; successor capitals include Prague, Belgrade and Zagreb

entityBefore.name_vi: Quân chủ Áo-Hungary

entityAfter.name_vi: Các quốc gia kế thừa Áo-Hungary

causes: Military defeat and armistice in World War I
National councils proclaimed sovereignty and withdrew allegiance from Habsburg institutions

power.note: Successor-state laws diverged; women's suffrage was adopted in some, not all, states.

governance.note: This is a composite event; Hungary briefly became a republic, while the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes was a monarchy.

territorialChanges.to: Hungarian People's Republic (later Kingdom of Hungary)

territorialChanges.territory: Croatia-Slavonia, Slovenia, Bosnia-Herzegovina and other South Slavic lands
territorialChanges.to: State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs; later Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes

events.note: No single date captures the dissolution. Successor proclamations occurred between October and December 1918; treaties later formalised borders.

events.capitalHistorical: Ankara (national movement); Istanbul (Ottoman court until abolition)

entityBefore.name_vi: Đế quốc Ottoman

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ

causes: Defeat and partition pressure after World War I
Turkish National Movement and War of Independence
Grand National Assembly abolished the Sultanate

power.note: Republican sovereignty was declared; actual pluralist elections evolved later.

church.note: Secularisation proceeded in stages; caliphate abolished 3 March 1924.

territorialChanges.note: Lausanne Treaty signed 24 July 1923; republic proclaimed 29 October.

events.note: Sultanate abolished 1 November 1922; Republic proclaimed 29 October 1923. These are distinct legal milestones.

events.capitalHistorical: Nanjing (provisional government); Beijing (after Yuan Shikai transfer)

entityBefore.name_vi: Đại Thanh

entityAfter.name_vi: Trung Hoa Dân Quốc

causes: Wuchang Uprising and provincial secessions
Collapse of Qing authority and negotiated abdication

power.note: Republican institutions were proclaimed; political participation remained limited and unstable.

territorialChanges.note: Qing abdication on 12 February formalised the end of the dynasty; frontier control and later warlord fragmentation remained contested.

events.note: The Republic was inaugurated 1 January 1912; the Qing abdication edict followed 12 February 1912. Do not collapse these dates.

entityBefore.name_vi: Trung Hoa Dân Quốc (chính quyền đại lục)

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Nhân dân Trung Hoa

causes: Resumption and victory of the Chinese Civil War by the Chinese Communist Party
Collapse of Nationalist control over mainland China

power.note: The PRC established Communist Party-led people's democratic dictatorship; current enum cannot express one-party state.

economy.note: Nationalisation and planning were implemented progressively, not all on proclamation day.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Nhà nước độc đảng
proposedLawChanges.description: Communist Party leadership constitutionally and institutionally monopolises national political direction.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Kinh tế kế hoạch hóa tập trung
proposedLawChanges.description: State ownership of major productive assets and binding national plans, consolidated in the 1950s.

territorialChanges.note: The ROC government retreated to Taiwan and continued to exist; this is not a universally recognised extinction of the ROC.

events.note: PRC proclaimed 1 October 1949. The ROC continued in Taiwan; treat sovereignty/recognition as contested rather than a seamless rename.

entityBefore.name_vi: Mạc phủ Tokugawa

entityAfter.name_en: Empire of Japan under Meiji Restoration
entityAfter.name_vi: Đế quốc Nhật Bản thời Minh Trị Duy Tân

causes: Tokugawa political crisis after forced opening to foreign powers
Satsuma-Chōshū alliance and transfer of governing authority to the Emperor

power.note: Meiji oligarchs centralised authority in the imperial state; the 1889 Constitution later created a restricted Diet.

trade.note: Unequal treaties and managed opening replaced sakoku.

events.note: Restoration edict dated 3 January 1868; civil war and dismantling of domains continued through 1869–71. Do not make all reforms instantaneous.

entityBefore.name_en: Empire of Japan under Meiji Restoration
entityBefore.name_vi: Đế quốc Nhật Bản thời Minh Trị

entityAfter.name_en: Empire of Japan under the Meiji Constitution
entityAfter.name_vi: Đế quốc Nhật Bản theo Hiến pháp Minh Trị

causes: Meiji state's centralisation and promise of constitutional government
Drafting and promulgation of an imperial constitution

power.note: The Diet existed but franchise was initially restricted to tax-qualified men; Emperor retained sovereignty.

events.note: Constitution promulgated 11 February 1889; entered into force with the first Imperial Diet on 29 November 1890.

entityBefore.name_en: Empire of Japan under the Meiji Constitution
entityBefore.name_vi: Đế quốc Nhật Bản theo Hiến pháp Minh Trị

entityAfter.name_en: Japan under the Constitution of Japan
entityAfter.name_vi: Nhật Bản theo Hiến pháp Nhật Bản năm 1947

causes: Defeat and surrender in World War II
Allied occupation and constitutional reform

power.note: Women obtained the vote in 1945; use proposed universal_suffrage to represent the 1947 constitutional order.

governance.note: Emperor retained as symbol of the State, sovereignty vested in the people.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Phổ thông đầu phiếu phổ quát
proposedLawChanges.description: Equal voting rights for adult citizens, including women.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Từ bỏ chiến tranh theo hiến pháp
proposedLawChanges.description: Article 9 renounces war and prohibits maintaining war potential; distinguish from ordinary disarmament.

events.note: Constitution promulgated 3 November 1946 and entered into force 3 May 1947. The emperor's constitutional role was transformed, but the monarchy was not abolished.

entityBefore.name_en: Kingdom of Spain under Alfonso XIII
entityBefore.name_vi: Vương quốc Tây Ban Nha dưới thời Alfonso XIII

entityAfter.name_vi: Đệ nhị Cộng hòa Tây Ban Nha

causes: Monarchist defeat in municipal elections in major cities
King Alfonso XIII left Spain and republic proclaimed

power.note: Women gained the vote in the 1931 Constitution, with first national general election voting in 1933.

events.note: 14 April is the proclamation date; Constitution adopted in December 1931.

events.capitalHistorical: Burgos (Nationalist headquarters during war); Madrid after victory

entityBefore.name_vi: Đệ nhị Cộng hòa Tây Ban Nha

entityAfter.name_vi: Nhà nước Tây Ban Nha dưới quyền Franco

causes: Military coup of July 1936 and ensuing Spanish Civil War
Nationalist victory with Axis assistance and collapse of Republican resistance

governance.note: The Francoist state did not function as a monarchy until the 1969 succession designation; monarchy is an imperfect enum fallback.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Nhà nước độc tài một đảng
proposedLawChanges.description: FET y de las JONS and Francoist institutions dominate; other parties prohibited.

events.note: Franco declared victory 1 April 1939; the dictatorship began through a 1936 military uprising and wartime consolidation, not solely on this date.

entityBefore.name_vi: Nhà nước Tây Ban Nha dưới quyền Franco

entityAfter.name_en: Kingdom of Spain in democratic transition
entityAfter.name_vi: Vương quốc Tây Ban Nha trong quá trình chuyển đổi dân chủ

causes: Death of Francisco Franco
King Juan Carlos I and reformist political actors opened a legal transition

power.note: 1977 elections and 1978 Constitution restored democratic elections; use universal_suffrage proposed value.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Phổ thông đầu phiếu phổ quát
proposedLawChanges.description: Adult citizens vote without sex-based exclusion.

events.note: Franco died 20 November 1975; Political Reform Act 1977, elections 15 June 1977, Constitution approved by referendum 6 December and promulgated 27 December 1978.

entityBefore.name_en: Empire of Vietnam / French colonial administration
entityBefore.name_vi: Đế quốc Việt Nam / chính quyền thuộc địa Pháp

entityAfter.name_vi: Việt Nam Dân chủ Cộng hòa

causes: Japanese surrender and collapse of wartime colonial authority
August Revolution and transfer of power by revolutionary committees

power.note: The 1946 general election was universal suffrage; constitutional equality declared irrespective of sex.

territorialChanges.from: French colonial and Japanese wartime administrations
territorialChanges.note: The declaration did not immediately end French control or create uncontested effective sovereignty over the entire territory.

events.note: Independence declared 2 September 1945; nationwide universal-suffrage election held 6 January 1946.

entityBefore.name_en: Vietnam under the First Indochina War settlement
entityBefore.name_vi: Việt Nam trong bối cảnh dàn xếp sau Chiến tranh Đông Dương lần thứ nhất

entityAfter.name_en: Democratic Republic of Vietnam (North); State of Vietnam (South)
entityAfter.name_vi: Việt Nam Dân chủ Cộng hòa (miền Bắc); Quốc gia Việt Nam (miền Nam)

causes: French defeat at Dien Bien Phu
Geneva Conference settlement and temporary military demarcation

power.note: North and South developed different political systems; this event is not a single national law transition.

territorialChanges.from: French Union / State of Vietnam control
French Union / State of Vietnam control
territorialChanges.to: State of Vietnam, later Republic of Vietnam

events.note: Geneva settlement described the line as provisional and envisaged nationwide elections in 1956; do not encode the 17th parallel as a permanent international border.

events.capitalHistorical: Saigon; Hanoi remained capital of DRV

entityBefore.name_vi: Việt Nam Cộng hòa

entityAfter.name_en: Democratic Republic of Vietnam authority over the South
entityAfter.name_vi: Chính quyền Việt Nam Dân chủ Cộng hòa tại miền Nam

causes: Collapse of South Vietnamese armed forces and government
North Vietnamese military offensive culminated in the fall of Saigon

power.note: South Vietnamese state institutions ceased functioning; national reunification was formalised in 1976.

events.note: 30 April 1975 marks the fall of Saigon and collapse of the Republic of Vietnam; formal state reunification followed in 1976.

entityBefore.name_en: Democratic Republic of Vietnam and southern transitional administration
entityBefore.name_vi: Việt Nam Dân chủ Cộng hòa và chính quyền chuyển tiếp miền Nam

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Xã hội Chủ nghĩa Việt Nam

causes: End of Republic of Vietnam government and national reunification election
First unified National Assembly adopted state name and institutions

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Nhà nước độc đảng
proposedLawChanges.description: Constitutional leading role of the Communist Party of Vietnam; one-party national political system.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Kinh tế kế hoạch hóa tập trung
proposedLawChanges.description: State-directed allocation and production planning, especially after reunification.

events.note: National Assembly adopted the name Socialist Republic of Vietnam on 2 July 1976.

entityBefore.name_vi: Đế quốc Nga

entityAfter.name_vi: Chính phủ Lâm thời Nga

causes: World War I military and supply crisis
Mass strikes, mutiny and loss of elite support

power.note: Provisional Government committed to Constituent Assembly elections; women participated in 1917 political process.

events.note: Gregorian date 15 March 1917 (2 March Old Style) is Nicholas II's abdication; February Revolution terminology follows Julian calendar.

entityBefore.name_vi: Chính phủ Lâm thời Nga

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Xã hội chủ nghĩa Xô viết Liên bang Nga

causes: Provisional Government's failure to end war and resolve land/food crisis
Bolshevik-led seizure of key Petrograd institutions

power.note: Soviet sovereignty was declared; effective political power concentrated in Bolshevik party structures during consolidation.

economy.note: Decrees began nationalisation and socialisation; central planning was not yet the mature 1930s system.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Nhà nước độc đảng
proposedLawChanges.description: Single party holds effective monopoly of state power; formal soviet institutions remain.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Kinh tế xã hội chủ nghĩa nhà nước
proposedLawChanges.description: Land nationalisation and state control of major industry; later evolves toward central planning.

events.note: 7 November Gregorian = 25 October Julian. RSFSR state formation was declared in the revolutionary period; the 1918 Constitution was adopted 10 July 1918.

events.capitalHistorical: Moscow (capital transferred from Petrograd in March 1918)

entityBefore.name_vi: Cộng hòa Xô viết Nga

entityAfter.name_en: Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic under 1918 Constitution
entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Xã hội chủ nghĩa Xô viết Liên bang Nga theo Hiến pháp 1918

causes: Bolshevik consolidation after October Revolution
Civil War and need to institutionalise Soviet authority

power.note: Constitution defined Soviets as state authority but excluded former exploiting classes from political rights.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Kinh tế xã hội chủ nghĩa nhà nước
proposedLawChanges.description: Land declared national property; banks and major productive assets moved to state control.

events.note: The 1918 Constitution proclaimed a federation of Soviet national republics. Wartime Communism and total central planning were later policy developments, not identical to the constitutional text.

entityBefore.name_vi: Cộng hòa Xã hội chủ nghĩa Xô viết Liên bang Nga

entityAfter.name_vi: Liên bang Cộng hòa Xã hội chủ nghĩa Xô viết

causes: Bolshevik victory in the Russian Civil War
Constitutional agreement among Soviet republics around the RSFSR

power.note: Formal federation of republics with a Communist Party monopoly in practice.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Nhà nước liên bang độc đảng
proposedLawChanges.description: Union of constituent Soviet republics under a single ruling Communist Party.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Kinh tế kế hoạch hóa tập trung
proposedLawChanges.description: National production and investment directed by central state plans; mature form established later.

territorialChanges.territory: RSFSR, Ukrainian SSR, Byelorussian SSR and Transcaucasian SFSR
territorialChanges.note: The 1922 founding Union included four founding units; subsequent Union republics joined later.

events.note: Union treaty/declaration adopted 30 December 1922; 1924 Constitution formalised the federal structure. The founding USSR is not identical to the Russian Empire.

entityBefore.name_en: Union of Soviet Socialist Republics under the 1924 Constitution
entityBefore.name_vi: Liên Xô theo Hiến pháp 1924

entityAfter.name_en: Union of Soviet Socialist Republics under the 1936 Constitution
entityAfter.name_vi: Liên Xô theo Hiến pháp 1936

causes: Stalin's consolidation of power
Forced collectivisation and rapid industrialisation under Five-Year Plans

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Nhà nước độc đảng
proposedLawChanges.description: Communist Party leadership is constitutionally and practically dominant.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Kinh tế kế hoạch hóa tập trung
proposedLawChanges.description: State ownership of major industry, collective farms and binding national economic plans.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Hệ thống lao động do nhà nước điều phối
proposedLawChanges.description: Employment and labour allocation subject to state planning and coercive controls; not equivalent to ordinary free labour.

events.note: Constitution formally proclaimed the USSR a socialist state and promised rights; actual political repression and purges are not represented by constitutional text alone.

entityBefore.name_en: USSR under late Brezhnev and Andropov/Chernenko stagnation
entityBefore.name_vi: Liên Xô thời kỳ trì trệ cuối Brezhnev và các nhiệm kỳ kế tiếp

entityAfter.name_vi: Liên Xô thời kỳ Cải tổ và Công khai hóa

causes: Economic stagnation and structural inefficiencies
Leadership change under Mikhail Gorbachev

press.note: Glasnost relaxed censorship progressively, with widening public debate.

economy.note: Perestroika introduced enterprise autonomy and market-like elements but did not immediately replace the planned economy.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Chuyển đổi kinh tế thị trường định hướng xã hội chủ nghĩa
proposedLawChanges.description: Partial enterprise autonomy, cooperatives and limited market mechanisms within a socialist framework.

events.note: Gorbachev became General Secretary 11 March 1985. Perestroika/glasnost were multi-year processes, not a single legal event.

entityBefore.name_en: USSR with constitutional Communist Party monopoly
entityBefore.name_vi: Liên Xô với độc quyền lãnh đạo của Đảng Cộng sản theo hiến pháp

entityAfter.name_en: USSR with multiparty political competition legally permitted
entityAfter.name_vi: Liên Xô cho phép cạnh tranh chính trị đa đảng về mặt pháp lý

causes: Glasnost and public pressure for political pluralism
Competitive elections to Congress of People's Deputies in 1989

power.note: Article 6 was amended to remove the constitutional monopoly; suffrage and elections became more competitive.

press.note: Legal and practical liberalisation continued; censorship did not vanish instantly.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Cộng hòa tổng thống đa đảng
proposedLawChanges.description: Competitive parties and a presidency coexist with a union-level federal constitution.

events.note: Article 6 amendment adopted 14 March 1990. Do not treat this as USSR dissolution; the Union persisted until December 1991.

entityBefore.name_vi: Liên bang Cộng hòa Xã hội chủ nghĩa Xô viết

entityAfter.name_en: Independent successor states of the USSR
entityAfter.name_vi: Các quốc gia độc lập kế thừa Liên Xô

causes: Failed August 1991 coup accelerated the loss of central authority
Union republics declared sovereignty/independence and formed the CIS
Belavezha and Alma-Ata agreements rejected the 1922 Union Treaty

economy.note: Successor states adopted different economic paths; market transition was not instantaneous.

territorialChanges.note: The Baltic republics restored independence in 1990–91; Ukraine, Belarus and Russia were central signatories. Russia continued the USSR's UN seat by international practice.

events.note: Distinguish de facto collapse/resignation (25 December), Belavezha agreement (8 December), Alma-Ata declaration (21 December) and formal USSR termination recognised by Declaration 142-N (26 December 1991).

entityBefore.name_en: Grand Duchy of Finland within the Russian Empire
entityBefore.name_vi: Đại công quốc Phần Lan thuộc Đế quốc Nga

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Phần Lan (quốc gia độc lập)

causes: Russian imperial collapse and competing claims to sovereignty after February Revolution
Finnish Parliament adopted declaration of independence

power.note: Finland's 1906 reform had already established universal and equal suffrage including women.

events.note: Independence declaration adopted 6 December 1917; civil war followed in 1918; republican constitution adopted in 1919.

entityBefore.name_vi: Ba Lan Quốc hội dưới quyền Nga

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Ba Lan

causes: Collapse of the partitioning empires after World War I
Józef Piłsudski took military command and then civil authority

power.note: Women obtained voting rights in 1918.

territorialChanges.territory: Former Russian, German and Austro-Hungarian Polish lands
territorialChanges.note: Borders were not settled on 11 November; territorial consolidation continued through 1921.

events.note: 11 November is the commemorated restoration date; Piłsudski notified foreign governments on 16 November.

events.capitalHistorical: Vilnius (claimed); Kaunas (temporary capital during Polish control)

entityBefore.name_en: German-occupied Lithuanian lands within the former Russian Empire
entityBefore.name_vi: Các vùng đất Litva bị Đức chiếm đóng, trước đó thuộc Đế quốc Nga

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Litva

causes: Collapse of Russian imperial authority
Lithuanian Council's national self-determination movement under German occupation

power.note: Democratic constitutional institutions were established later; women gained suffrage.

territorialChanges.from: German military occupation / former Russian Empire
territorialChanges.note: Effective sovereignty required subsequent diplomatic and military struggle; independence restored 11 March 1990.

events.note: The declaration is a clear founding act, but not the date of complete effective control.

entityBefore.name_vi: Đế quốc Nga / lãnh thổ Estonia bị Đức chiếm đóng

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Estonia

causes: Russian Revolution and collapse of imperial authority
Estonian Salvation Committee proclaimed a republic before German occupation

power.note: Constituent Assembly and democratic constitution followed in 1920.

territorialChanges.note: German occupation followed immediately; effective government began after German withdrawal in November 1918.

events.note: Republic officially proclaimed 24 February 1918; War of Independence continued until 1920.

entityBefore.name_vi: Đế quốc Nga / các vùng đất Latvia bị Đức chiếm đóng

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Latvia

causes: Russian imperial collapse
German defeat and withdrawal
Latvian People's Council proclaimed a republic

power.note: Constituent Assembly elected in 1920.

events.note: Proclamation date 18 November 1918; War of Independence delayed full consolidation until 1920.

entityBefore.name_vi: Đế quốc Nga / Chính phủ Lâm thời Nga

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Nhân dân Ukraina

causes: February Revolution and formation of the Central Rada
Bolshevik ultimatum and outbreak of the Ukrainian-Soviet War

power.note: The Central Rada's republican programme included broad electoral rights.

territorialChanges.note: The Central Rada's Fourth Universal was dated 22 January and proclaimed independence on 25 January; Ukrainian statehood was contested in the ensuing war.

events.note: This is a multi-stage and contested state-building process; Soviet Ukraine was proclaimed separately by Bolsheviks in Kharkiv in December 1917.

entityBefore.name_vi: Ấn Độ thuộc Anh

entityAfter.name_vi: Liên bang tự trị Ấn Độ

causes: British withdrawal after World War II
Political deadlock and Mountbatten Plan partitioned British India

power.note: The 1947 dominions inherited limited franchise; universal adult suffrage followed under later constitutions.

governance.note: Dominions remained constitutional monarchies under the British Crown until republican constitutions.

territorialChanges.territory: Western Punjab, Sindh, NWFP and East Bengal (with boundary details)
Remaining British Indian provinces and princely states acceding to India

events.note: Independence dates are 14 August for Pakistan and 15 August for India; Radcliffe boundary award was published 17 August.

entityBefore.name_en: Korea under Japanese colonial rule and Allied occupation
entityBefore.name_vi: Triều Tiên dưới ách thuộc địa Nhật và sự chiếm đóng của Đồng minh

entityAfter.name_vi: Đại Hàn Dân Quốc

causes: Japanese surrender and division of occupation zones at the 38th parallel
Failure of US–Soviet joint arrangements and separate elections

power.note: Constitutional republic established in the South; democratic practice was imperfect under early presidents.

events.note: Separate states were proclaimed 15 August (South) and 9 September (North) 1948; both claimed legitimacy over all Korea.

entityBefore.name_vi: Đế quốc Nga

entityAfter.name_en: Russian Empire after the Emancipation Reform
entityAfter.name_vi: Đế quốc Nga sau Cải cách Giải phóng nông nô

causes: Defeat in the Crimean War exposed institutional and military weaknesses
Serfdom constrained agricultural productivity and state modernisation

labor.note: The Emancipation Manifesto freed privately held serfs in 1861; land redemption obligations and communal restrictions continued.

events.note: The 3 March 1861 date is Gregorian (19 February Old Style). Emancipation was phased and did not immediately eliminate all peasant obligations or state peasant dependencies.

entityBefore.name_en: Grand Duchy of Finland under the Russian Empire
entityBefore.name_vi: Đại công quốc Phần Lan thuộc Đế quốc Nga

entityAfter.name_en: Grand Duchy of Finland with unicameral parliament and universal suffrage
entityAfter.name_vi: Đại công quốc Phần Lan với nghị viện đơn viện và phổ thông đầu phiếu

causes: 1905 general strike and constitutional crisis in the Russian Empire
Finnish Parliament Act replaced the four-estate Diet

power.note: The game enum is male-specific; Finland's reform enfranchised women and men equally and allowed women to stand for election.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Quyền công dân và bầu cử bình đẳng
proposedLawChanges.description: Equal political rights for women and men, including voting and eligibility for elected office.

events.note: Parliamentary reform adopted in 1906; first elections were held in March 1907. Finland was still a Russian Grand Duchy, not yet independent.

entityBefore.name_en: United States before the Social Security Act
entityBefore.name_vi: Hoa Kỳ trước Đạo luật An sinh Xã hội

entityAfter.name_en: United States with federal social insurance framework
entityAfter.name_vi: Hoa Kỳ với hệ thống bảo hiểm xã hội liên bang

causes: Great Depression and mass unemployment
Federal response to old-age poverty, unemployment and dependent families

economy.note: This is a broad mapping only; the Act created social insurance and grants, not a planned economy.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Bảo hiểm xã hội và nhà nước phúc lợi
proposedLawChanges.description: Publicly mandated social insurance, old-age benefits, unemployment protection and family support.

events.note: The Social Security Act was signed 14 August 1935; it created old-age benefits, unemployment insurance and aid programmes. It is a representative welfare-policy milestone, not the origin of all US welfare policy.

entityBefore.name_en: United Kingdom before post-war welfare settlement
entityBefore.name_vi: Vương quốc Anh trước dàn xếp phúc lợi hậu chiến

entityAfter.name_en: United Kingdom with National Health Service and expanded social insurance
entityAfter.name_vi: Vương quốc Anh với Dịch vụ Y tế Quốc gia và bảo hiểm xã hội mở rộng

causes: Beveridge Report and wartime social-policy debate
Labour government implemented National Health Service and National Insurance legislation

economy.note: Public provision expanded; this does not mean the UK became a planned economy.

proposedLawChanges.name_vi: Y tế phổ quát và bảo hiểm xã hội
proposedLawChanges.description: Universal public health service and broad social insurance coverage.

events.note: The National Health Service Act was passed in 1946 and the NHS came into operation on 5 July 1948. The National Insurance Act 1946 was a parallel pillar.
